question: The simple interest (in ₹) on ₹5,000 at 5% per annum for 2 years is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Total effective interest rate for 2 years = Rate × Time = 5% × 2 = 10%

Simple Interest = 10% of Principal

SI = (10 ÷ 100) × 5000 = 500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹5,000

Rate (R) = 5% per annum

Time (T) = 2 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 
 ₹5000
 Principal
 
 
• 
 

 
 5% p.a. for 2 years
 Total Interest = 10%

 
 ₹500
 Simple Interest

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI = (5000 × 5 × 2) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = (5000 × 10) ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 50000 ÷ 100

⇒ SI = 500

**∴ The correct answer is ₹500.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Compound Interest (CI)

When interest is compounded annually, Amount (A) = P × (1 + R÷100)T and CI = A − P.

Difference between CI and SI

For 2 years, the difference between CI and SI on a certain principal P at a rate of R% is given by the formula: Difference = P × (R÷100)².

Amount in Simple Interest

The total amount at the end of the period is the sum of principal and interest: A = P + SI = P × [1 + (R × T)÷100].
